question: A 2-year-old girl has had three febrile UTIs. Ultrasound shows mild left hydronephrosis and MCUG confirms grade III VUR on the left. Which investigation should now be performed and why?

answers.text: Repeat MCUG in 6 months to re-grade the VUR

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Repeat MCUG too early does not add information; VUR can self-resolve. The priority now is to detect scarring before deciding on long-term prophylaxis or ureteric reimplantation.

answers.text: DMSA renal scintigraphy to detect cortical scarring and quantify differential renal function

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. DMSA is the gold standard for detecting renal cortical scarring. It quantifies differential function and identifies segments at risk — findings that directly determine whether ureteric reimplantation or long-term prophylaxis is needed.

answers.text: MRI urography without contrast as a radiation-free alternative to DMSA

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: MRI urography can image the tract but requires sedation in young children and does not provide the functional radionuclide data of DMSA. DMSA remains the standard for scar detection in this scenario.

answers.text: CT urography to assess the full urinary tract in detail

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: CT urography is not indicated here. It adds significant radiation to a young child without answering the specific question (scarring and differential function) that DMSA addresses.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember the tool-to-question mapping: DMSA = scar detection + differential function. With recurrent febrile UTI and confirmed VUR, DMSA is now the investigation of choice to guide definitive management.
Well done. DMSA answers 'has the kidney scarred?' — the critical question when deciding long-term management of recurrent febrile UTI with confirmed VUR.
